title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
label: "Wild Thing" Jonnie Adonis

won.source: Won the 30-man over-the-top battle royal at the federation's first pay-per-view, March Mayhem.

lost.source: The federation's own broadcasts still bill him as champion through the 5 April title tournament finals and call him the former champion by the following Thursday's show (10 April); the vacating itself is not carried by any surviving document.

note: The vacated title was to be awarded by a three-way match, held at the next pay-per-view.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
label: El Perfecto

won.source: Won a triangle match over Patty Babes Carter and the Heartbreaker at W.A.R. to fill the vacant championship.

note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, the Heartbreaker, who is billed as champion by 1 July 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
label: Chris Hunter

won.source: Won a six-man, two-ring open-barbwire steel-cage elimination match, "Hardcore Hell," at Cage Wars.

note: Cage Wars itself does not survive in the held record; only its announcement and its aftermath do. Still billed champion on 18 November 1997. No title-change document survives for the transition to the next and final champion, Lord Doomsday, sometime before 3 December 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
label: the Heartbreaker

won.source: Billed as HCW World Champion on the allied WOWA's own 1 July 1997 broadcast; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, Chris Hunter, who wins the title at Cage Wars on 14 September 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
label: Lord Doomsday

won.source: Billed champion by the federation's final pay-per-view, November Armageddon, on 3 December 1997; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

note: Retained the title against Chris Hunter in a Dog Collar Texas Tornado double-cage match that ended in a one-hour draw at November Armageddon, the federation's final pay-per-view — the last champion of record before the federation's closure.

won.source: Won the finals of a 32-entrant tournament run across three broadcasts.

lost.source: Lost the title to "Franchise" Shane Dreamer at W.A.R.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-us
label: "Franchise" Shane Dreamer

won.source: Defeated Jon Stilwater for the title at W.A.R.

note: The federation's own later commentary recalls Cyanide beating him for the title "the first week he came here," though the transition itself is not carried by any surviving document.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-us
label: Cyanide

won.source: Billed as champion at Mega Fight (24 May 1997), where he retained the title in a three-way match over Mammoth and Mike "The Mechanic" Malone; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

note: Still champion when the federation retired this title on 23 July 1997, replacing it with the new Television Championship.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tv
label: "Vile" Vince Viper

won.source: Won the eight-man tournament final over Patty Babes Carter at British Invasion to become the first Television Champion.

note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, Austin Starr, who is billed champion by September 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tv
label: Damon Zex

won.source: Crowned champion on the federation's 18 November 1997 broadcast.

note: A defense against Angus was announced for the federation's next Thursday broadcast on 3 December 1997; no result survives.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tv
label: Austin Starr

won.source: Billed champion by September 1997, chased by challenger Sammy the Kid; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, Damon Zex, on 18 November 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-hardcore
label: Flash Flood

won.source: Won a "Hardcore Search" held on the federation's earliest cards; already billed champion by the federation's own 30 March 1997 broadcast.

note: Retained the title against Gunloc in a ladder match at W.A.R. Named the federation's own longest-reigning champion and its Best Title Holder at the 25 April award show. No title-change document survives for the transition to Lord Doomsday, attested by 24 May 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-hardcore
label: Lord Doomsday

won.source: Billed as the current champion at Mega Fight (24 May 1997), where he retained the title against Immorality; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

note: Also retained the title against Austin Starr at Beachblast on 27 July 1997, holding both this title and the World Heavyweight Championship at once.

won.source: Won a tournament final across a two-part Thursday Night Thunder broadcast.

lost.source: Both wrestlers were fired for disrupting a pay-per-view; the titles were declared vacant.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tag
label: Terrorize & Stryfe

won.source: Won a multi-team match over FIRE and the Party Animals at W.A.R. to fill the vacant titles.

note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champions, the Party Animals, on 24 May 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tag
label: the Party Animals (Sam & Gabe)

won.source: Won the titles at Mega Fight.

note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champions, Double Impact, attested by September 1997.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tag
label: Double Impact (Steven Stryfe & Tyson Tercell)

won.source: Billed as champions on the federation's 12 and 24 September 1997 broadcasts; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

note: The federation's own 24 September broadcast calls them its "ONLY two time champions," implying an intervening loss and regaining of these titles that no surviving document in the held record carries. A defense against Tha Horsemen took place at the federation's final pay-per-view; the announcing team's own talk of "a rematch" afterward suggests they retained.

title: hcw-hardcore-1997-triangle
label: Immorality

won.source: Named the first-ever HCW Triangle Champion in a segment of the Beachblast broadcast.

lost.source: A tournament to decide a new champion was announced for the federation's 15 October 1997 broadcast; its outcome does not survive in the held record.

note: The same Beachblast broadcast's own commentary elsewhere calls Chris Hunter "still HCW Triangle Champion" in an earlier segment — an inconsistency in the federation's own record that this collection preserves rather than resolves.
